ingredients: 3 yellow, red or orange bell peppers (diced)
1 tbsp dried Italian seasoning (more to taste)
⅛ tsp crushed red pepper (adjust to taste)
28 oz can of crushed tomatoes (with Italian spices added–like basil, oregano, etc. if you can find that)
1 cup shredded parmesan or Italian four cheese blend
steps: Cook the lasagna noodles for about 2-3 minutes less time than the package directions say (leave them slightly al dente).
Once they’re done, lay them flat on foil and set aside.
Quarter all 4 zucchini and thinly slice.
Dice all 3 bell peppers and mince 3 cloves of garlic
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat, saute the garlic, half the diced onion, all of the zucchini and all of the bell peppers together.
Add the baby spinach at the end (when the zucchini/red pepper are almost done cooking), saute another 3 minutes until spinach is wilted.
Sprinkle Italian seasoning, salt, and crushed red pepper to taste on top, stir, and let it cook a couple more minutes. Then remove from heat.
Mince 3 cloves of garlic.
Spray a medium sized saucepan with cooking spray and lightly saute the garlic and remaining red onion until the onion is translucent.
Add the crushed tomatoes.
Add Italian seasoning to taste, if your crushed tomatoes don't have that already added.
Once the sauce is heated through, turn the heat down on low.
Combine 1.5 cups of the ricotta cheese and 1 cup of the mozzarella in a bowl. Keep the Parmesan cheese (or Italian blend, if using) separate.
Spray the bottom of a large casserole dish with cooking spray.
Put a layer of sauce at the bottom of the dish (For every layer of sauce, I used 1/2 the self-made sauce and 1/2 the pre-made sauce)
Put a layer of the lasagna noodles.
Put another layer of the sauce (1/2 pre-made, 1/2 self made).
Put a layer of the veggies.
Take the cheese mixture, and put little crumbles of the cheese mixture all over the veggie layer (don’t try to spread it out, the little crumbles seemed to work well).
Put another layer of the lasagna noodles.
Layer of sauce.
Layer of veggies.
Cheese mixture crumbles.
Layer of lasagna noodles.
Layer of sauce.
Sprinkle 1 cup of the Parmesan cheese (Or Italian Cheese blend) all over the top.
Cover with foil and bake at 350 degrees for 30 min.
Uncover and bake for 5 min. longer until the cheese has melted.

steps: Wash and dry all of your fruit before beginning. Pull the grapes from their stems.

Make the Faces: This is the most important part! Arrange the three rice cakes on your board. I like to stagger them. Place two blueberries for eyes on each of the rice cakes. Add the cashew for the nose, the sliced pepper for the mouth, and the olive slices for the eyebrows.

Add the Hair: Place the thin peach slices in a cascade from the top of the first rice cake to the middle to create Sarah's hair. Layer the peach slices for a better effect. Now, arrange the raspberries in two cone shapes on top of the third rice cake. I start with four raspberries on each side, followed by three, two, and one. For Mary's hair, use the blackberries to shape a swirling cone on the third rice cake. Add some blueberries or concord grapes to add texture and fill any holes.

Add the Bodies/Dress: First, add the concord grapes for Sarah's dress. Add as many as you like in a triangular shape trying to fill in any gaps or holes. Next, add the green grapes for Winifred's dress in the same manor, followed my using the red grapes for Mary's dress.

Filling in the Background: If you have space on your platter, you can fill it with other ingredients. I suggest black olives on the top of the platter for a night sky and pretzels on the bottom for the ground. This is optional. You could add some small pumpkins to the platter to give it an autumn vibe. Serve and enjoy!

pe-homemade-baby-teething-biscuits.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: 2 small ripe bananas (or 1 large ripe banana (should be 6oz total in weight)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F or 170 degrees C.
Place the oats into a food processor and blend to form a fine powder.
Add all other ingredients and blend until a dough has formed.

Remove mixture from the food processor and roll in between 2 sheets of parchment paper to approx. ¼ inch thick. (Note: it's really important to get it to ¼ inch thick - if the dough has been rolled thicker than 1/4 inch in thickness it will take longer to cook).
Remove the top layer of paper and cut into 36 evenly sized sticks.
Place the sheet of cut teething sticks onto a baking sheet and bake for 12 minutes until just cooked through.

Take the teething sticks out of the oven. Run a knife along the slice marks and separate each teething stick. Bake them again for another 10-15 minutes to make them firm. Make sure to keep an eye on the sticks as they bake, and remove any that are cooking quickly to stop them from burning.
Remove and cool completely on the baking sheet before transferring them to a cooling rack. This is important to make sure they don't end up being chewy vs. crunchy!

pe-homemade-cinnamon-toast-crunch.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: 2 tbsp aquafaba (can also use water or maple syrup)
steps: Add the rolled oats to a high speed food processor and blend until finely processed.
Next, add all remaining cereal ingredients to the bowl of a food processor. Start with ½ tbsp of water and adjust if needed.
Blend to form a dough that’s easily rollable. If the dough is too dry add a little more water.
Place the dough in the fridge for 30 mins to chill.
While the dough is chilling, prepare the cinnamon sugar by mixing the coconut sugar and ground cinnamon in a small bowl.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F / 180 C.
Divide the dough in half. Roll one half of the dough in between 2 sheets of parchment paper until very thin. The thinner the dough is rolled the crispier it will be when cooked.
Remove the top sheet of parchment paper, trim the edges of dough forming a rectangle.
Lightly brush with aquafaba and then sprinkle with ¼ of the cinnamon sugar, gently press into the dough.
Place the parchment paper back on top of the dough and flip the dough over. Remove the top layer of paper, brush with aquafaba and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar.
Using a knife or pizza cutter, cut the dough into ¼ inch squares.
Carefully transfer to a baking sheet and bake for 6-8 minutes.
Remove and allow to cool before separating the squares.
Repeat with remaining dough.
Serve with your favorite chilled milk.
Store the cereal in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

ingredients: ½ cup unsweetened almond milk or lowfat milk, warm (118 ml)
¼ cup brown sugar (unpacked) or coconut sugar (can also use powdered stevia (55 grams)
¼ cup vegetable oil (Use any vegetable oil like sunflower, coconut oil or canola/rapeseed oil) )
1 tsp vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
½ cup pure pumpkin puree (110 grams)
3½ cups whole wheat bread flour, sifted, divided (440 grams) Note - you'll need more for hands and work surface)
¼ cup butter, softened at room temperature (60 grams)
½ cup coconut sugar or brown sugar, unpacked (can also use powdered stevia (100 grams)
2 tbsp raisins, dried cherries, walnuts, pecans, or dried cranberries (optional)
2 tbsp unsweetened almond milk or lowfat milk
steps: In a small bowl add warm milk, sugar and sprinkle the yeast on top. Let it rise for 5minutes.
In a large mixing bowl combine the oil, egg, vanilla, pumpkin puree and mix until smooth and well combined.
Pour in the milk with yeast and stir until combined.
Add the flour and spices and stir until incorporated.
Knead by hand or using a mixer for 3-5 minutes until you have an elastic and smooth dough.
Form into a ball and transfer to a lightly greased bowl. Cover with a kitchen towel and let it rise for 1 - 2 hours until doubled in size.
Transfer the dough onto a floured surface. With the help of a rolling pin, roll out the dough until you have a 14×16-inch rectangle.
Spread the butter on top and sprinkle with sugar, cinnamon and pumpkin spice. Roll the dough into a log and with a knife cut out 12 rolls.
Place the rolls into a 9x13 inch baking pan and cover again. Let them rise for 30 minutes, then preheat your oven to 350 degrees.
Take the rolls to the oven and bake for 20-30 minutes until golden brown on top.
To make the glaze, mix the icing sugar with milk and vanilla. Top the cinnamon roll with glaze and enjoy!

ingredients: 1 cup whole wheat self rising flour
½ cup low fat plain Greek yogurt
steps: Add all ingredients into a medium mixing bowl and mix to form a dough. Add up to ½ tablespoon of water to the mixture if a little dry.
Turn out onto a lightly floured work space, counter, or cutting board and gently knead to bring the mixture together.
Allow the dough to rest for 5 minutes before using.
Roll dough on a lightly floured surface. Dough can be rolled into a 10 inch round and topped with your favorite pizza toppings before baking in the oven.

To bake, once you have added toppings straight onto the uncooked, rolled out pizza base, bake the pizza in the oven at 390-400 degrees F for 15-20 minutes. If you want a crunchier crust, pre-bake the dough for 5-10 minutes at 390-400 degrees F for 10 minutes, then add the toppings and bake for an additional 8-15 minutes until all of the ingredients have cooked through.

steps: Bring water to a boil in a Dutch oven; add kale. Cover and cook over medium heat 5 minutes or until tender. While the kale is cooking, chop the rest of your veggies. Remove kale with a slotted spoon, reserving cooking liquid. Chop kale and set aside.
Add potato to reserved cooking liquid in pan; bring to a boil. Reduce heat, and simmer 10 minutes or until tender. Drain; partially mash potatoes. Stir in kale and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Preheat oven to 400°. Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt, diced onion, and chopped sage. Cook 13 minutes or until browned.
Combine potato mixture, onion mixture, green onions, and pepper in the pan. Remove from heat; cool slightly.
Divide potato mixture into 8 equal portions, shaping each into a 1/2-inch-thick patty. Place patties on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray.
Bake at 400° for 20 minutes. Then broil patties for 5 minutes or until browned.
You can serve the patties as is, or top them with 1 Tbsp fresh grated parmesan, or serve them with ketchup, or just garnish them with sage sprigs: you can really do anything you like with them!

steps: Add the water and sweetener to a pot. Bring to a boil, about 5 minutes. Boil over medium heat an additional 5 minutes.

pe-red-lentil-dal.creator: thepickyeater
steps: Mix the ginger garlic, curry powder, coriander, garam masala and crushed red pepper in small bowl and set aside.

Heat a large soup pot over medium heat. Add your oil, onions and celery and cook on medium high heat for about 2 minutes until vegetables are fragrant and translucent. Stir occasionally to prevent burning.

Turn down heat and add the ginger, garlic and spice mix and cook on low heat for about 1 minute, allowing the spices to “bloom” until they become fragrant. Add the lentils, vegetable stock, salt, diced tomatoes and coconut milk.

Bring up to a boil, then reduce heat to a low simmer. Cook with a lid on for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally until lentils are soft. If your heat is up too high, the liquid will evaporate before the lentils are done cooking. If that happens, just add a little bit more stock (or water, if you are using that) and continue to cook. When lentil are soft, turn off your heat and add in your chopped cilantro. Adding cilantro at the end will keep the flavor lively and fresh.
Serve as a soup, or over brown rice with some steamed veggies, or with naan or roti! I chose to have ours as a "stew" over brown rice.

steps: Start by preparing the salted caramel. In a non-stick saucepan heat the sugar and water over medium heat. Stir until combined.

Let the sugar change color to amber.
Once the sugar reaches the amber colour takes off the heat and immediately pour in the heavy cream and stir until combined. Be careful the mixture will start to bubble a lot.

Transfer the crust into a 9 inch / 23 cm springform cake pan. Press into the bottom of the pan and let it set in the fridge while you are making the filling.

In a separate bowl mix the cream cheese, sour cream, powder sugar, salted caramel and vanilla extract and mix until combined.
Fold in the whipped cream and mix until just combined.
Pour prepared filling into a springform cake pan and spread evenly across the crust.
Place in the refrigerator overnight or at least 8 hours.
Before serving top the chilled cheesecake with swirls of salted caramel and sprinkle with sea salt flakes.

They’re packed with hearty roasted sweet potatoes, protein-rich refried black beans, and warm spices, all wrapped up in soft corn tortillas and topped with a creamy, spiced yogurt sauce.
ingredients: cilantro (diced (it’s a garnish, so use as much as you like)
⅛ tsp cayenne pepper (optional, if you like it spicy)
keywords: sweet potato and black bean tacos
sweet potato tacos with black beans
web.name: Sweet Potato Tacos
steps: Cut up your veggies: sweet potatoes, onions, and carrots. Meanwhile, heat the black beans over low heat and add 2 tsp taco seasoning (or to taste - the more you add, the spicier it will be).

Saute the onions, carrots, sweet potatoes in olive oil over medium heat. Add in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and cayenne if you’re using it. Let the mixture cook until the potatoes are soft. (If you want it to cook quickly, cover the pan and just stir every couple minutes)
While the veggies are cooking, chop your cilantro and set aside.

Prepare your yogurt sauce. Empty the Greek Yogurt into a bowl, and stir in 2 tsp of taco seasoning (taste it periodically to make sure it’s achieved the spice level you want). Add 1-2 Tbsp water to thin out the yogurt mixture (the more water you add, the thinner it will get). Mix everything together until the yogurt is smooth.

Begin assembling your tacos! Heat up your corn tortillas, and on each tortilla put: 2-3 Tbsp refried black beans, 1/3 cup of the veggie mixture, 1-3 Tbsp of the yogurt mixture (depending on how much sauce you want), and a sprinkle of cilantro.

steps: Heat oil in a large pot on high heat.
Add cumin seeds and as soon as they start popping, add onion, garlic and ginger and sauté over medium-low heat until caramelized, about 5 minutes.

Add the water, chickpeas and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer and cover. Cook on low for 30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes or so to make sure the Chana Masala doesn't stick to the bottom of the pot.

pe-vegan-baked-potato-soup.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: 6 cups chopped red or yukon gold potatoes (, or other type you prefer (about 6 medium potatoes or 2 pounds)
1 cup chopped sweet or yellow onion
drizzle of oil or broth to sauté
4 cups veggie broth (, low sodium if needed)
¾ -1 teaspoon sea salt (, adjust for your preference)
½ - 1 cup raw cashews (, or cashew powder (see note)
vegan bacon (, my recipe or any vegan bacon you prefer)
steps: Sauté potatoes, onion, carrots and celery with a drizzle of oil or broth until softened and fragrant. About 7-8 minutes.
Add 4 cups broth and salt and bring to a rapid boil. About 5-7 minutes.
Once it boils, cover, reduce to a low simmer and cook for about 15 minutes until potatoes are soft and can be pierced with a fork.

When tender, carefully take out 4 cups of the soup avoiding the carrots and put it in a blender. You want to be careful not to get many carrots because the soup will end up with an orange tinge. It will be hot so be extra cautious.
Add the cashews (or powder) and lemon and blend until smooth and creamy. Add back into the pot and mix in the pepper.
Serve with toppings of choice!

ingredients: 8 cups popcorn (salted gives best end result)

½ - ¾ cup chopped nuts (optional but give a yummy crunch (salted nuts add extra flavor)
steps: Preheat the oven to 250 degrees F / 120 C.

Make caramel according to the recipe but only thicken on the shorter side (about 5 minutes). Once thickened remove from heat and add in the baking soda with the vanilla and salt. You will see it bubbling but this is what helps it be more spreadable.
Add popcorn to a large bowl, with the caramel and nuts (if using). Mix around to coat well.
Spread popcorn mixture out on a parchment lined cookie sheet.
Bake for an hour, mixing around every 15 minutes.
Once done, remove from the oven and allow to cool. Once cool you can break it apart.
Serve! Stores crisp in an air tight container!

pe-vegan-carrot-cake-cupcakes.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: Grated carrots, shredded coconut, and chopped walnuts for topping
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees and line a muffin pan with cupcake liners.
Whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat together the vegetable oil and sugar until well combined. Add the applesauce and vanilla and mix until combined.
Add the dry ingredients to the oil mixture and mix until smooth.
Fold in the grated carrots and chopped walnuts.
Fill each cupcake liner 2/3 full of batter. Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 30 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
To make the icing, beat together the vegan butter, vegan cream cheese, and vanilla extract until smooth. Add the powdered sugar and beat until combined.
When the cupcakes are cooled completely, pipe the icing on top and garnish with grated carrots, shredded coconut, and walnuts.

pe-vegan-carrot-dogs.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: 1 cup veggie broth (low sodium if needed)
¼ cup tamari (or soy sauce if not gluten-free)
steps: Cut the ends off of the carrots and shape into hot dog like shapes using your vegetable peeler if preferred for aesthetics.

Boil the carrots for about 10 minutes until you stick a fork in them and it goes in but still has some give. I put the carrots in water over medium high heat (before the water was boiling) and it took 10 minutes total.
While boiling, mix all marinade ingredients in a deep dish or plastic Ziploc bag.
When carrots are done boiling, run them under cold water then add them to the marinade. Marinate for at least 30 minutes but overnight is best for optimum flavor.
Cook the carrot dogs on a pan over medium high heat until browning on the outside, about 3-5 minutes. Make sure to move them around so they char on all sides.
You can also BBQ them on a grill, about 5-7 minutes until charred on all sides. I like to baste them with the marinade as they cook.

You can also roast them in the oven at 400 degrees F / 205 C. For this option you can skip boiling them and simply put them in the oven with marinade in a foil covered baking dish. Bake for about 20 minutes, then uncover and bake for another 10 until you put a fork in them and they still have some give.
Top with what you prefer and enjoy!

web.name: Vegan Chickpea Blondies
steps: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F / 190 C.
Put flours, baking powder and salt in a large bowl and whisk to break up clumps.
Put maple syrup, chickpeas, almond butter and vanilla into a food processor. You can use a blender too if you prefer. Blend until smooth.
Add the blended mix into the bowl with the flour and mix until combined.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour into a prepared square baking dish (9x9 or 8x8 works).

Mix cocoa powder, chocolate chips, baking powder and salt in a bowl breaking up clumps.

Prep your ramekins with a spray of oil, rub around to coat. Then dust each with a little cocoa powder.
Split the batter into the ramekins.

Bake for 15 minutes. Allow to cool a bit, but enjoy warm.

pe-vegan-churros.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: ¼ cup water or dairy-free milk (see note)
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F / 120 C.
Add flours, starch, sugar, salt and cinnamon in a bowl. Whisk to mix and break up any clumps.
Make a little well in the middle and add in the apple sauce and water/milk. Mix again to combine and get a smooth batter.
Allow to set in the fridge for at least 10 minutes. The longer it sets the more firm your dough so the round like shape will keep better when baked.

Fill a pastry bag with a large tip, or a plastic bag with the edge cut off. You want at least a 1 inch hole, but any size will work as long as you remember you will get less or more depending on the size.
Squeeze out pieces onto a parchment lined baking sheet. I made mine about 3 inches long. Use a knife to cut off the batter in between pieces.

Bake for 15 minutes, until golden. To keep them from getting one flat edge, start flipping them on each side starting at about 5-6 minutes when they have baked enough to turn without falling apart. You can turn on all the sides by turning every few minutes until you get to 15 or they are golden on each side.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a bowl. Then mix the cinnamon and sugar in another bowl.
Once baked, allow the churro pieces to cool. This will help them set more.
One by one, dip them in the butter then roll in the sugar mixture.
Enjoy as is or dip in melted chocolate or caramel.

ingredients: 6 cups vegan mashed potatoes (, homemade or store-bought)
1½ cup chopped sweet or yellow onion
drizzle of your favorite oil to sauté (, or broth if oil free)
½ cup dry lentils (, green or brown (use more if not using chickpeas, see note)
1½ cup cooked chickpeas (, drained and rinsed (optional, see note)
4 cups veggie broth (, low sodium if needed)
2-4 tablespoons Yondu umami seasoning (, can sub soy sauce or tamari (see note)
steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F / 205 C.

You can either chop the whole mixture in a food processor after cooking, or simply just chop the chickpeas and walnuts into smaller pieces using a food processor now. I prefer to do this because it’s easier to clean up.
Sauté onion, garlic and salt with oil, or broth if oil free, over medium heat until onion is soft. About 5 minutes.
Add the lentils, chickpeas, walnuts, parsley and thyme and saute until just browning. About 3-5 minutes.
Add 2 cups of the broth, Yondu and tomato paste and cook covered for about 8-10 minutes. Don’t let it burn.
If you opted to chop the entire mixture, then chop now in a food processor. Make sure to pulse slowly so it doesn’t turn into mush. It helps to do it in small batches. Add back to the pan when done.
Add the carrots, peas and the rest of the broth into the pan and cook until most of the liquid has evaporated but it still has some sauce.
Spread at the bottom of a square baking dish. Then top with the mashed potatoes.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the top is browning at the edges.
Allow to cool so it sets better and serve!

steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 C).
Put oat flour, almond flour, potato starch, baking powder, sea salt and ground mustard into a medium mixing bowl. Whisk until combined and there are no clumps.
Make a little well in the middle of the mixed dry ingredients. And pour in milk and vinegar.
Slowly combine with a spoon or spatula, mix until just combined but don’t over mix. Fold in cheese if using.
Allow to sit for a few minutes, use this time to put away the ingredients, put used items in the sink and wipe off the counters.

Bake for 28-30 minutes, ovens vary but you want them crisp on the outside. You can broil for 2-3 minutes to get the browned tops if you want them. They will cook more as they cool.
Serve with butter if desired!

Using a food processor, coarsely chop the chickpeas until crumbled like a meaty texture.
Set aside. Then chop the mushrooms in the same way.
Sauté the garlic in broth or oil until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook until the liquid has evaporated, about 5 minutes.

Fill the peppers with the mixture and put on the tops. You can also drizzle with a tiny bit of oil if you want.
Bake for about 30-35 minutes until just browning on top.
Serve and enjoy!

pe-vegan-gluten-free-sugar-cookies.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: 1 cup oat flour (gluten free if needed )
1 ¼ cup almond flour (make sure it’s the super fine kind )
½ cup butter (dairy free if needed, softened but not melted)
4 tablespoons water (adjust for the thickness you want)
2 teaspoons maple syrup (this helps the icing stick better to the cookies)
½ teaspoon vanilla extract (don’t use if you want pure white icing)
gel food coloring and sprinkles to decorate (optional)
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F / 175 C.
Put flours/starch, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Whisk well to remove clumps and combine.
In another bowl, add sugar, softened butter and vanilla. Beat with a hand or stand mixer (using the whisk attachment) until fluffy.
Add in the flour mixture as you mix and continue to mix until it is combined well. Switch to a paddle attachment if using a stand mixer.

Knead with hands until you get a ball, then wrap in plastic and chill for at about 15-20 minutes. I tested working with it right away and it actually worked well. It was a little fragile so I made sure I only rolled the dough out to no less than ¼ inch.

Once chilled, put the dough on a piece of parchment paper, then place another piece on top. Using a rolling pin, roll out the dough. Ideally you want it to be no less than ¼ inch thick or the shapes will get pretty delicate and hard to move to the cookie sheet.

Use cookie cutters to cut out cookies. Place cookies on a parchment lined baking sheet. Carefully peel away the scraps and use them to form another ball and then repeat the process of rolling it out, cutting out shapes, and forming a ball until you are left with very little to no dough. If the dough softens too much (it can happen if you are working in a warm area), then place the parchment with cookies in the fridge to harden a bit so you can peel them off the parchment without them breaking. You can also place a hand under the parchment paper and lift the cookie that way.
Bake cookies for 10-11 minutes until golden at the edges. Mine took 10 minutes. Allow to cool completely before removing or they will break. At least 10 minutes.

If you plan to make the icing, once cookies are completely cool (the next day is best), prepare the icing by mixing icing ingredients in a bowl with a whisk until smooth. Add gel food coloring if using and mix in.

To ice the cookies, I found it easiest to dip the tops (flat side down) into the bowl very carefully so you just get icing on the tops, then put them on a plate, rack or back on the cooled baking sheet to harden. Allow the icing to drip off the tops before turning them back up or it could run off the sides. You may need to keep whisking the icing as it could form a crust on the top depending on how fast you work. You can also put the icing in a piping bag and decorate that way.
If you are decorating the cookies make sure to put sprinkles, etc on top while the icing is wet and not hardened. Or decorate as you prefer.

ingredients: 1 cup vegan butter (Earth Balance or similar brand)
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Combine the non-dairy milk and apple cider vinegar in a bowl. Whisk together and set aside for 10 minutes. This creates vegan buttermilk.
Combine the all-purpose flour, cacao powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Whisk together to combine.
Combine the vegetable oil, sugar, and vanilla extract in a large bowl. Whisk together to combine. Add the vegan buttermilk. Whisk together until completely combined.
Pour the dry ingredients into the bowl with the wet ingredients. Stir until combined. Don't overmix.

Line the muffin tin with cupcake liners. Fill the liners 3/4 of the way full. Bake for 18-20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Allow the cupcakes to cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.
Bring the vegan butter to room temperature. Do not melt the butter. It must be at room temperature.
Whip the butter with a mixer at medium speed until creamy.
Add the powdered sugar 1/2 a cup at a time until it is absorbed before adding the next cup until all of the sugar has been added.
Add the non-dairy milk one tablespoon at a time, whipping as you go. Add the vanilla extract. and continue to whip until the buttercream is light and fluffy.
Transfer 1/3 of the frosting to another bowl. Add the green food coloring and stir until the desired color is achieved.

ingredients: ½ cup almond milk or other dairy free milk (, divided into 2 and 6 tablespoons)
¼ cup fresh lemon juice (, divided)
2 tablespoons lemon zest (Meyer lemons work best)
½ teaspoon lemon zest (Meyer lemons work best)
steps: Turn up the heat on your griddle, you want it nice and hot for cooking the pancakes. You know it’s ready when you spray some water on it and you hear it sizzle. Also if it is not non stick you should use a spray oil to avoid the pancakes sticking.
Put the oat flour, potato starch, baking powder and 1/8 teaspoon salt into a bowl and mix well.
Put almonds into a food processor and blend until they are finely ground.
Add 2 tablespoons milk, 3 tablespoons maple syrup, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, vanilla extract and the other 1/8 teaspoon salt. Blend until combined. This is the "ricotta."

Dig a small well in the flour mixture and add the "ricotta" mixture into the well. Next add the 6 tablespoons left of milk, the other 3 tablespoons of maple syrup, the other 2 tablespoons of lemon juice and the lemon zest.
Slowly mix until well combined, do not overmix but make sure there are no clumps. Allow to settle a few minutes so the mixture can fully combine.
Drop spoonfuls (about ¼ cup each) onto the griddle. Cook about 4-5 minutes on each side. They should be slightly brown when ready and come off the griddle easily.
While the pancakes are cooking, make the lemon glaze if using. Whisk powdered sugar, lemon juice and lemon zest in a bowl until smooth.
Allow the pancakes to cool a bit before eating, this lets the texture settle and fully develop. Drizzle with lemon glaze, maple syrup or anything else you prefer and devour!

pe-vegan-pigs-in-a-blanket.creator: thepickyeater
ingredients: 4 veggie dogs or carrot dogs (, gluten-free if needed (see note)
1 cup almond flour / almond meal (, see note)
steps: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F / 190 C.
Whisk all batter ingredients in a shallow dish.

If your tortillas aren’t soft and pliable, warm them by wrapping them in a damp paper towel and placing them in the microwave for 30 seconds. Check and if not warm and soft, warm for 15 second increments until they are. If you don’t have a microwave, then steam them using a double boiler.

Cut the hot dogs into 3 equal pieces. Slice the tortillas into 4 equal strips. You can trim the hot dogs and tortillas any way you want to make them fit. If you want them pretty, then cut the strips a little smaller than the hot dog pieces so they show at each end.
Dip each tortilla strip in batter, making sure both sides are covered. Allow to soak for about 30 seconds to get them nice and soft. Don’t leave them too long or they will fall apart.
Roll up a hot dog piece in a strip of tortilla sealing the end. It should stick since it is wet.
Place on a parchment lined cookie sheet. Repeat with each piece.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until browning on the edges. You can cook longer if you want them more crisp.
Enjoy warm! Dip in ketchup and mustard.

steps: Preheat the oven to 320 degrees F / 160 C. Line a 9” x 5” loaf pan with baking paper.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Set aside.
In a separate bowl whisk together the melted vegan butter, vanilla extract, vegan sour cream and almond milk.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and mix until combined. Do not over mix the batter.

Transfer the batter to the prepared tin and bake in the oven for 50-60 minutes or until an inserted skewer comes out clean. After cooking for 30 minutes place a sheet of foil over the top of the cake to stop it from browning too quickly.
When cooked, remove and allow to cool in the tin for 10 minutes before cooling completely on a cooling rack.
To prepare the glaze, mix the powdered sugar and 1 tbsp almond milk together in a small bowl until smooth. Adjust thickness by adding more almond milk if you’d like a thinner glaze.
Once the cake is completely cold drizzle the glaze over top.
Store the cake in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 F/ 175 C
Combine dry ingredients in a bowl and whisk to make sure to break up any clumps.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredient mix, and add the wet ingredients.
Mix until combined.

Place large spoonfuls of the batter into muffin tins lined with baking cups. Fill about 3/4 of the cup. I use foil baking cups as they don’t stick like paper does and also they don't trap in the moisture like paper does. If you use paper the end result will be a little more wet.

Bake for 19 minutes. Depending on your oven, your baking time may vary by a minute or two. Start checking them at 17 minutes and take them out when the tops begin to get firm and a toothpick comes out clean. Let cool in the muffin tins. Once cool to the touch, remove and continue cooling on racks until completely cool, about an hour.

ingredients: 6 tablespoons almond flour (, make sure it is fine grained)

web.name: Healthy Vegan Pumpkin Cupcakes
steps: Preheat oven to 350 F/ 175 C
Combine dry ingredients in a bowl and whisk to make sure to break up any clumps.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredient mix, and add the wet ingredients.
Mix until combined.

Place large spoonfuls of the batter into muffin tins lined with baking cups. Fill about 3/4 of the cup. I use foil baking cups as they don’t stick like paper does and also they don't trap in the moisture like paper does. If you use paper the end result will be a little more wet.

Bake for 19 minutes. Depending on your oven, your baking time may vary by a minute or two. Start checking them at 17 minutes and take them out when the tops begin to get firm and a toothpick comes out clean. Let cool in the muffin tins. Once cool to the touch, remove and continue cooling on racks until completely cool, about an hour.
After cupcakes are cooled, you can frost.
Enjoy! If stored in a plastic or glass container with a little bit of airflow, these will still be good the next day!

tt-7238220546020871467.caption: These easy protein boost tofu balls are very popular blw snacks in Korea 👀♥️ Here’s the recipe: You need one pack of firm tofu, rice flour, and veggies of your choice (or you can skip veggies). I used beets, carrots and spinach for colors! ♥️🧡💚 You can add some cheese as well. 1. Remove excess water from tofu, pat it dry with paper towel. 2. Cut tofu into 4 pieces. 3. Add one piece of tofu into blender with 3 tablespoons of rice flour and a handful (~1/4 cup) of veggies. 3. Blend until you get to doughy texture. 4. Repeat 2&3 with the remaining pieces of tofu. 5.  Turn them into bite sized ball shapes. 6. Bake at 325F for 10-15 min, or until the surface becomes non-sticky.  I also added some parmesan cheese to enhance flavor, but it’s entirely optional!  . . . #blw#babyledweaning#tofurecipes#veganrecipes#vegancooking#cooking#cookwithme#toddlersnacks#healthysnacks#easyrecipes#babyfood#toddlerfood#toddlermenu#kidsbreakfast#nycmom#momtips#momhacks

tt-7366094195238456619.caption: Joomukbap is a Korean style rice ball — literal translation is “fist rice”, because the rice ball is the size of a fist! This meal is easy to make, yet super nutritious. You have your vegetables, meat, grains and fat/oil. Below is the recipe! I prefer 1 to 1 ratio of cooked rice to all other ingredients (veggies + meat). Below is what I used:   * 2 cups of cooked rice (Short-grain rice or sushi rice works best, because they are sticky. Jasmine rice or long rice are less sticky and will not work) * 1 cup of cooked ground meat + seasoning (I used ground beef, and added 1 tablespoon of soy sauce), for younger babies, skip seasoning.  * 1 cup of cooked, chopped vegetables (I recommend carrots, broccoli and mushroom — less moisture, easier to shape) * Mix cooked rice, cooked meat, and vegetables in a bowl * Add and mix in 1 tablespoon of Sesame oil * Shape the mixture into balls! * Optional: shred roasted seaweed in a bowl, roll the rice ball and cover it with the seaweed  Feel free to season as desired for older toddlers, kids & adults. Adding 1-3 tablespoons of soy sauce will enhance flavor.  #babyfood#BLW#helathyrecipes#balancedmeals#healthymeal#koreanrecipes#asianfood#toddlermeals#babymeals#toddlersnacks#schoollunch#lunchideas#lunchideasforkids#kidsmeal

tt-7429373037293849902.caption: Does your child love candy? Remember these 3 things! 🍫 Control over timing - by deciding when your child can have candy, you can avoid sugar rushes at the worst times, like right before bed or during school hours. Pair candy with protein - when candy is paired with a protein, like nuts or milk, it slows the sugar absorption, helping your child avoid the highs and lows of a sugar crash. Avoid the “Forbidden Fruit” effect - letting your kids enjoy candy without a lot of restrictions makes it less of a “forbidden fruit.” This helps them develop a healthier relationship with sweets, where candy isn’t off-limits, but just another treat they can enjoy when properly balanced with other foods. Ready to have more control over the food in your home without adding more stress to your day? I create easy, healthy, plant-based meals so you don’t have to! tt-7429415471419624746.caption: For my toddler’s lunch today, I made a Korean traditional banchan called Hobak Jeon (Zucchini Fritters), and here’s the recipe! 1. Slice zucchini into 1/4 inch thick slices 2. Prepare a plastic bag with 3 spoons of flour 3. Place zucchini slices into the plastic bag and shake to coat each slice with flour  4. In a bowl, beat 2 eggs and add 1 tablespoon of sesame oil     5. In a skillet on medium heat, add 1 tablespoon of oil. Once hot, dip one floured zucchini slice into the egg wash and place on the skillet to cook. Continue until the pan is filled  6. Cook on each side until both sides are golden brown (1-2 minutes per side)  I used Eggland’s Best Eggs to enhance taste & for better nutrition – Eggland’s Best Eggs have 6 times more Vitamin D and more than double the Omega-3, with 25% less saturated fat, compared to ordinary eggs.  #toddlermeals #blw #babyledweaning

tt-7447571681809304874.caption: 5 Signs You’re Not Eating Enough 🥗 Not eating enough can lead to some serious symptoms that affect your energy, mood, and overall health. Here's how to spot it and fix it: 🍽️ 1) Constant fatigue – If you're always tired, it could mean you're not getting enough calories or nutrients. Try adding more protein, healthy fats, and whole grains to your meals to boost energy. 💪 2) Irritability & mood swings – Low blood sugar from under-eating can cause mood shifts. Keep snacks like nuts or fruit handy to stabilize your blood sugar levels throughout the day. 🍎 3) Hair loss or thinning – Lack of key nutrients like iron and vitamins can cause hair issues. Focus on nutrient-dense foods like leafy greens, nuts, and eggs. 🥗 4) Difficulty concentrating – Not eating enough can affect your brain function. Eat regular, balanced meals to improve focus and clarity. 🧠 5) Frequent hunger pangs – Always hungry? This means your body isn’t getting the fuel it needs. Add more fiber and protein-rich foods to stay full longer. 🍗 Fix this by eating nutrient-dense meals consistently. Start nourishing your body right today. tt-7456848729300290862.caption: The biggest misconceptions about veganism? 🌱 While a vegan lifestyle can be incredibly nourishing and packed with health benefits, simply cutting out animal products doesn’t guarantee a balanced diet. A healthy vegan diet still requires planning and an understanding of essential nutrients. Here’s why: - Protein Matters: When you’re eating vegan, protein can be trickier to get, but it’s still key for energy, muscle health, and feeling full. Adding foods like lentils, tofu, quinoa, and chickpeas ensures you’re getting enough of this essential macronutrient. - Healthy Fats Are Essential: Many vegan diets can be low in healthy fats, which are critical for brain function, hormone balance, and energy. Avocados, nuts, seeds, and olive oil are great sources of these fats. - Balanced Nutrition: Whole foods, veggies, and fruits are the base of a healthy vegan diet, but variety matters too. To avoid relying on processed vegan options, fill your meals with colorful produce, whole grains, and plant-based proteins. Eating vegan doesn’t mean automatic health—it’s about making smart food choices and ensuring your body gets the nutrients it needs to thrive. So if you’re vegan or considering going vegan, take the time to learn about balanced, nutrient-rich meals. Overwhelmed? tt-7460560138907176238.caption: Our go-to snack that’s super quick & easy yet delicious & nutritious:  - 2-3 spoons of non-fat Greek yogurt  - With flax seeds, chia seeds, hemp seeds, and sunflower seeds  - Along with  @ikigai_fruits that are naturally sweet & delicious Flax seeds, chia seeds, hemp seeds, and sunflower seeds are excellent sources of healthy fats and essential minerals for supporting rapid brain growth.  The key is to serve with fruits that are naturally sweet and delicious so that there’s no need for added sugar.  The natural sugars in fruit are accompanied by fiber and other nutrients, which slow down the absorption of sugar into the bloodstream. This makes fruit less likely to cause blood sugar spikes compared to added sugars.  I love serving @ikigai_fruits as their fruits are exceptionally tasty with premium quality, sourced from small Japanese farms known for craftsmanship and innovation to preserve quality.  #workingmom #wfh #nycmom #toddlereats #toddlersnacks #blw #babyfood #healthysnacks #easysnacks #snacksforkids #snackideas

tt-7463157296785263914.caption: Kitchen Hacks From A Gluten-Free Vegan Health Coach💚 1️⃣ Rolled oats instead of processed breakfast cereals Why? Many cereals are full of refined flours, added sugars, and artificial additives. Rolled oats are gluten-free, nutrient-dense, and a healthier choice! 🌱 2️⃣ Tempeh instead of processed plant-based meats Processed vegan meats can have refined flours, hydrogenated oils, and excess salt. Tempeh is a fermented, protein-packed, and fiber-rich option. 💪 3️⃣ Whole grain gluten-free bread instead of white bread White bread is made with refined flour that spikes blood sugar and lacks nutrients. Whole grain bread is full of fiber and keeps you satisfied for longer! 🍞 4️⃣ Homemade hummus instead of store-bought spreads Many store-bought spreads contain unhealthy oils, additives, and too much salt. Homemade hummus is fresh, simple, and healthier! 🥙 Trying to eat healthier without extra effort? tt-7475665360113372462.caption: Picky eating isnt “just a phase”! ⚠️  If anyone has told you that picky eating is a phase and will pass, they’re wrong. But with the right approach, you can make your child a more adventurous eater with healthier eating habits! 1) Start by introducing new foods gradually and pairing them with familiar favorites. 2) Make mealtime enjoyable by involving your child in meal prep and letting them choose between options. 3) Keep portions small to avoid overwhelming them, and avoid pressure or negativity around food. Remember, it’s about creating a positive relationship with food, and change can take a long time! So be consistent, celebrate small victories, and remain patient. video.narration: Let's see what's inside orange Gatorade. It starts with water, sugar, and then dextrose, which is another type of processed sugar, and those are the first three ingredients. And then citric acid and sodium citrate, which are types of preservatives derived from citrus fruits. Salt for electrolytes. Monopotassium phosphate, which is adds potassium, another electrolyte. Gum arabic, which is used as a stabilizer and an emulsifier to keep the ingredients from separating. Natural flavors. Sucrose acetate isobuterate, which is also used as an emulsifier to keep the ingredients from separating. Glycerol ester of rosin, another stabilizer and emulsifier. And yellow six, which is artificial food coloring. I'm not sure I would go to Gatorade as a source of electrolytes.

video.narration: Let's see what's inside White Monster. It starts with carbonated water, then citric acid, which is a preservative, then erythritol, which is a sugar, alcohol, and artificial sweetener made by fermenting corn or wheat, then torene, which is an amino acid added for mental alertness, sodium citrate, which is a preservative, natural and artificial flavors, Panix ginseng flavor, which comes from the ginseng root, L-carnitine L-tartrate, which is used for energy production, caffeine, sucralose, which is basically Splenda, sorbic acid, which is a preservative, benzoic acid, another preservative, niacinamide, which is a form of vitamin B3, decalcium pantothenate, which is a form of vitamin B5, aculfame potassium, which is an artificial sweetener, inostitol, which is a sugar, alcohol, and sometimes called vitamin B8, pyrodoxine hydrochloride, which is a form of vitamin B6, and cyanobalamin, which is a synthetic form of vitamin B12. If I want caffeine, I think I'll just drink coffee.

video.narration: My secret to getting veggies in without complaint is in this jar. Alright moms, let's make my go-to veggie pasta sauce. Sauce in some onion, carrot, broccoli and celery, all the good stuff they'd normally say no to. Then pour in one can of organic tomato sauce and fill the same can with water and chicken stock. Season it up with salt, black pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika and some herbs. You can be creative and add whatever seasonings you like. I also add some chickpea for extra protein, totally optional but so good. Let it cook for 5-10 minutes until the veggies soften, then let it cool down completely. Remove celery and blend it smooth. And that's it, a super creamy sauce that's perfect for pasta, rice or even pizza if you like.

video.narration: Let me show you how easy it is to plan your baby's weekly meals. Planning baby or toddler meals doesn't have to be complicated. I actually keep it really simple. Every Sunday I go over this little table I've created where I list all the food groups the baby need every day, like dairy, proteins, grains, healthy fats, etc. Then I fill in ingredients for each one for each day just to make sure I'm covering all the nutrition throughout the week. I start with whatever I have already at home and add the rest to my grocery shopping list. After that I either look for new recipes I want to try or stick to the ones I have or just keep it simple and steam those vegetables. Honestly babies don't need fancy meals unless that's what you want to do. Now when I make my baby's meals I don't force him to eat everything I just make sure I offer a good variety. This has made my week so much easier and it takes away all the stress of figuring out what to cook every single day. Trust me, plan by ingredients not by recipes it changes everything.

video.narration: No one talks about how emotional feeding kids can be and the anxiety you get when they don't want to eat. It's okay though, our job is just to make that meal and offer it. Today I am making quinoa with red lentils and carrots. For this recipe, you'll need half cup quinoa, half cup lentils, one cup vegetable broth, one cup water, and half cup small diced carrots. Bring it to a boil then lower the heat, cover, and let it cook. While that is cooking, I am mixing egg yolk, Greek yogurt, and flax seeds. My son loves anything mixed with Greek yogurt so I like to play around here. I am finishing up the meal with some oranges for vitamin C and there you go, a tasty plate that's ready to be ruined by a one year old.

video.narration: Here is everything my one-year-old ate today. He does wake up at 5 a.m. for a bottle and then he goes back to sleep until 7. His breakfast is very simple. He pretty much has the same thing every day because mornings are my busy time. I cannot make him a nice meal plus he's not that hungry. So today he's having a peanut butter toast and a boiled egg and this is how much he ate. That's a good start. For lunch I am making him steamed vegetables. He's been refusing broccoli lately although he used to love it but I'll keep adding it until he tries it again. On top of that I had some pasta leftovers from last night so I put it on the side and of course Greek yogurt and flaxseed. That's always a win and this is how much he ate. He still didn't touch the broccoli but that's okay. After lunch he takes a bottle and goes for a nap. Again keeping it simple with the snacks he's getting a pouch. For dinner of course I'm gonna give him the vegetables I made at lunch. I am not cooking twice. A boiled egg and some bananas. I always top everything with olive oil. It's the gold I add to the plate and this time he ate the broccoli so that's a win. After dinner it's a bottle and bed.

video.narration: Here is everything my one-year-old ate today. As always he takes a bottle at 5 a.m. and goes back to sleep until 7 30. You know we like to keep breakfast simple so today he's having oatmeal. I either do baby oatmeal or overnight oats. I like to add some chia seeds and top it with some berries. I ended up cutting the chicken into small pieces because it's easier for him to grab and this is how much he ate. After lunch he takes a bottle and goes for a nap. After he wakes up I give him a quick snack. Today he's having yogurt with flax seeds and peach. This will keep him full until dinner time. For dinner he's having chicken leftovers. I added some steamed broccoli with olive oil and bananas and yes I give him dinner right before he goes to bed. This is how much he ate. He's back to eating broccoli which is really good. We finish with a bottle and it's bedtime.

video.narration: Here is everything my 1 year old ate today. I like to plan his meals ahead of time. This saves me a lot of thinking and a lot of time. I have a table of ingredients I'm planning to use throughout the week and I use the recipe app to save recipes with those ingredients. I truly love this app because I can just import any recipe I want from anywhere to the app. That way I can have all the recipes in one place. I can also open the video from the app if I want to re-watch it again. And this is how much he ate for breakfast. At lunch I really wanted to try this new recipe with chickpea and sweet potato but it was a total mess so never mind backup plan it is. I quickly steamed some vegetables, a hard boiled egg and yogurt. I'm just glad I made it on time because this little one was really hungry. Anyway after lunch he had a bottle and took a nap. When he woke up I gave him some mangoes. It's a soft mango and he loved it. I really wanted to give him chickpeas for lunch because they are so good for babies and toddlers. And since that did not happen I am making him some improvised hummus. He's having that for dinner as a side dish with whatever we are having. Today it's green beans with tomatoes and garlic. After dinner he had another bottle and went to bed.

video.narration: Let's see what's inside Skippy peanut butter. It starts with roasted peanuts, sugar, 42 grams of added sugar which is almost as much as two full-size Snickers bars, hydrogenated vegetable oil which is a combination of cotton seed, soybean and rape seed oil to increase shelf life and salt. Why is all of this stuff in here? All you really need is peanuts and salt. That's it. Seeing ingredients like this is exactly why I teach people how to eat healthier without feeling overwhelmed. If you're ready to stop guessing and start eating with confidence, check out the Picky Eater Mastery, your step-by-step guide to simple plant-based eating. Link is in my bio.

tt-7616101337289346317.caption: Most kids snacks are just junk food with better packaging. 🙅🏽‍♀️ I've been a health coach for years and I still stop and read the label on almost everything before it goes in my cart.  The marketing on kids' snacks especially is designed to make you feel like you're making a good choice words like "natural," "made with real fruit," or "good source of protein" on the front while the sugar content on the back tells a completely different story. Here's what I actually look for: — Added sugar under 5g per serving — An ingredient list short enough to read in one breath — A real food as the first ingredient  — oats, nuts, fruit, not corn syrup or enriched flour Once you know what you're looking for, it takes about 10 seconds to make a better call right there in the aisle. The swap is almost always sitting right next to it on the shelf. Follow @pickyeaterblog for daily tips on feeding your family healthier options.

tt-7616516818164813070.caption: Most kids won't eat vegetables at breakfast. Mine ask for them. Here's how I got here 👇🏽 My kids have had steamed broccoli with breakfast since they started solids. They didn't come out of the womb easy eaters. I spent the first year of their lives deliberately training their palates, the same way you work on other skills like walking, sleeping, or using a fork. Most people assume picky eating is just a personality trait. It's really a habit that forms early, and it's one you can shape. The window between 6 and 10 months when you introduce solids is one of the most underrated opportunities you have as a parent. Keep offering. Keep varying. It doesn't happen overnight. My kids now eat everything healthy. That didn't happen by accident. Follow for daily tips on feeding your family healthier options.

And most of it isn't coming from candy. 👀 It's hiding in the "healthy" stuff. Flavored yogurt, granola bars, juice boxes, oatmeal packets. The front of the package says wholesome and the back tells a completely different story. The swap that makes the biggest difference at snack time is simpler than you'd think. Plain whole milk yogurt with fresh fruit on top instead of the flavored kind. Same creamy texture, way less sugar, and kids adjust to it faster than most parents expect. You don't need to overhaul everything at once. One swap repeated consistently adds up to a significant difference over a school year. Follow for daily tips on feeding your family healthier options.

tt-7622074259153702158.caption: Here's a made up rule you don't have to follow👇🏽 The idea that vegetables only belong at dinner. Nobody actually decided this. It just became the default and now most families are fighting a losing battle every single night trying to get their kids to eat something green after a full day of snacks and a plate of whatever else is on the table. My kids start every single morning with a plate of vegetables before anything else hits the table. S teamed broccoli, cucumbers, snap peas.  Whatever is in the fridge that day. If you wait until dinner to serve vegetables you're already behind... Think about it this way.... You wouldn't wait until 7pm to give your kids their first sip of water for the day.  Don't do that with vegetables either. The morning is actually the easiest time to get vegetables in.  Kids are hungrier, less distracted, and haven't filled up on anything else yet.  Once you shift the timing everything else gets easier. Start tomorrow. It takes two extra minutes and it changes the whole dynamic around food in your house. Follow for daily tips on feeding your family healthier options.

video.narration: The way I get my kids to eat their veggies, or the way I used to get my kids to eat their veggies, is I used to bribe them with dessert. I know it's like, you're not supposed to do that, right? Um, everyone tells you, don't bribe your kids with dessert because then the dessert is going to be elevated and the veggies are going to be seen as something that they just have to endure and dessert is actually the real reward. But really what I discovered in raising two picky eaters who are now great eaters is that it's not actually about the dessert, it's about the framing. So basically if you say eat your broccoli or you're not going to get any dessert, what your kid hears is that broccoli is bad and dessert is my reward and then you basically just end up having them hate broccoli even more because they have to get through that in order to get the thing that they really want. But what I did with my kids and what I've done with hundreds of kids in my time as a picky eating feeding coach, I tell them, hey look, like it looks like you feel really uncomfortable about this food, let's just say it's broccoli. You feel really uncomfortable about broccoli, like maybe you feel a little bit anxious about it, maybe you just are worried you don't like the taste or maybe you've had it before and you don't like the taste. And so, but it seems like you really like this particular snack or dessert or whatever it is, like whatever treat it is that they actually prefer. So then I say, hey, it looks like you feel really comfortable with this food, but you feel like really uncomfortable with this food. So what if we tried eating one bite of the food that you already feel comfortable with with this new food that you just don't really have a lot of experience with yet and sometimes it takes us time to be able to understand or appreciate new things and everyone has trouble with change. And so I understand, you know, why you might be having trouble with this new food. So to make it easier for you, I'm going to allow you to have this dessert or the snack or whatever it is that is something that they really, really enjoy. I'm going to allow you to have a little bit of this as long as you also try a little bit of that and whatever that is, whether it's a vegetable or a meal or whatever. And I would just alternate bites between the thing that they liked and the thing that I wanted them to try. And every time they had a bite of the thing they wanted that I wanted them to try, they get to have a bite of the thing that they want to have. And I did that with both of my kids and I've done that with hundreds of other kids in helping them to get them to try new foods and really like it's not about bribing with the dessert or the snack that they like. It's not that that thing is the reward. It's actually the bridge that helps them get more comfortable with eating new foods or trying new foods. If your kid has trouble eating vegetables or also only eats beige foods or has four foods that they want to eat and nothing else, try this trick. I'm telling you it will work. You just have to be consistent about it. And if you're a parent looking for picky eating support, follow me because I post helpful tips like this every single week.

tt-7624301279442914574.caption: If your kiddo STILL won't touch a veggie, this is your weekly reminder to keep trying!! Honestly, it can take over 100+ tries or exposures of a food before kids of all ages will want to actually eat it. While some resources say you only need to try 15-20 times, in my experience working with kids, and in getting my two picky eaters to eat veggies, it can literally take hundreds of times over months and months and months! While this can be super frustrating, this is typical, and totally normal.  That's because kids taste buds literally change every two weeks. And accepting a new food is so much more than just trying it. They have to feel comfortable with the food, they have to be ok with the texture, the flavor, etc. Getting through each of these steps can mean multiple exposures throughout the process.  So what should you do? Just keep giving it to them in small portions! Encourage them to take a "fairy bite" and let them alternate with a food that they feel comfortable with (ideally something healthy-ish, not dessert). And you should eat it alongside them to model behavior, AND don't make them a separate meal if they don't want to eat it. You can also get them involved in preparing it a bunch of different ways - sauteeing, steaming, roasting, as part of a dish, pureed into a sauce, etc. and have them try it all of those ways.  Just because they don't like it today, doesn't mean that's forever. My daughter literally took 12 YEARS to like blueberries. She also took 12 years to enjoy any type of smoothie. I'm not kidding. And what was the preparation for her that changed things? Mixing blueberries into a smoothie (two for one combo! 😅) If you're struggling with a picky eater in your house, follow for daily picky eating tips! #pickyeaters #pickyeatingtips #pickyeater

tt-7626477990490230030.caption: Chicken potato gratin 🤍 A cozy family dinner your toddler can actually enjoy. Ingredients: • 1 chicken breast • 1 egg yolk • 3 small/medium potatoes, peeled and sliced into thin rounds • 1 cup heavy cream • Butter • 1 handful mozzarella • 1 handful cheddar cheese Seasoning: • ½ tsp paprika • ½ tsp garlic powder • ½ tsp onion powder • ½ tsp oregano • ½ tsp dried parsley • Salt & pepper (salt only for 1+) Directions: Blend chicken, egg yolk, and seasoning. Form medium meatballs and keep 1 tbsp of the chicken mixture aside. Air fry the potato slices until cooked through. Cook the meatballs in butter on medium heat until golden, then remove. In the same pan, cook the remaining chicken mixture, then add heavy cream and mozzarella. Stir until thick. Layer potatoes, meatballs, creamy sauce, then cheddar cheese in an oven dish. Bake at 375°F (190°C) for about 10–15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden. Finish with parsley. tt-7628785522848075021.caption: This could be why your baby isn’t eating what you want them to eat, especially veggies … There are a handful of common reasons babies refuse food. Here are six I see most often: 1️⃣ They’re tired: Learning to eat takes coordination and focus. If your baby is exhausted, they may not have the energy to engage with food. ➡️ Try offering meals when your baby is well-rested and hungry! Like right after a nap. 2️⃣ They’re not feeling well: Appetite often drops when babies are sick or coming down with something. This is completely normal. ➡️ During illness, prioritize fluids and milk feeds. Once they’re feeling better, their appetite typically comes back. Stick with familiar foods and give it time. 3️⃣ Teething discomfort: Sore gums can make eating less appealing. ➡️ Offer soothing, cool foods like yogurt, cucumber, or chilled fruit. A cold teether before meals can also help reduce discomfort. You can also try offering frozen veggies to gnaw on! 4️⃣ Not hungry enough: If your baby isn’t showing interest, they might not be hungry enough, so they’re less motivated to try new foods. ➡️ Adjust timing of breastmilk or bottle feeds so they come to the table ready (but not desperate) to eat. 5️⃣ They want independence: Many babies prefer to take the lead with feeding and may resist being spoon-fed. ➡️ Let them explore by feeding themselves. You can hand them pieces of food or offer a preloaded spoon to support independence. 6️⃣ They’re still learning: Eating is a brand new skill, and some babies simply aren’t sure what to do yet. ➡️ One of the most effective ways to teach is by modeling. Let your baby watch you eat and eat with you, they learn a lot just by observing. Notice how none of these reasons has anything to do with your baby not liking the veggie or food you’re trying to serve them! Picky eating is often about a variety of things, not just the food. Which means that small adjustments to timing, environment, and approach can make a big difference over time!  If your baby isn’t eating, you’re not alone. Don’t give up and keep giving them the foods you want them to eat!   Follow for more daily feeding tips. #pickyeating #pickyeater

tt-7629499297217744141.caption: For years, I struggled with getting my kids to eat healthier foods. And I as picky eater coach I see this A LOT  I remember It felt like I was doing something, but it always ended in a power struggle, tears, and a totally stressed-out me. So for one week, I went cold turkey. No ‘one bite,’ no ‘try it for mommy,’ nothing. The first two days were… silent. And honestly, a little scary. I kept serving veggies with every single meal, just like always, but I didn’t say a word about them. I also didn’t give another option, but I did let my kids decide whether they wanted to eat the meal I was serving. My toddler barely touched them. And by day three, something I did not expect started to happen. My toddler, who would normally push the plate away, actually picked up a piece of broccoli. He didn’t eat it. He just looked at it. He squished it. The next day, he licked a carrot stick. By removing the pressure, I removed the fight.  He no longer had anything to push against. It turns out, our kids are naturally curious. When we turn mealtime into a battleground, their only goal is to win the battle. When we make it a safe space for exploration, their curiosity can finally take over and they can learn about foods at their own pace. 👋🏽 I’m a picky eater health coach helping families eat healthier and raise non picky eaters! Follow for more picky eater tips and easy solutions!

tt-7641397608174341389.caption: This is the healthy low sugar pancake recipe that converted my picky eater 🥞✨ These fluffy almond milk pancakes are the one breakfast my kids actually get excited about and they have NO idea they’re dairy-free and healthy! Made with unsweetened almond milk instead of regular milk, and minimal added sugar, they come out just as soft, fluffy, and golden as the classic version. Ready in 35 minutes, one blender, 10 pancakes. My secret tip: let the batter rest for 10 minutes before you cook. that’s the whole trick for getting that airy texture. Ingredients - 1¼ cups (150g) all-purpose flour use a gluten-free flour blend or oat flour for a gf option - 2 tsp baking powder - 1/4 cup coconut sugar - 1 cup (237ml) unsweetened almond milk - 1 room temperature egg can use a flax egg for a vegan option - 1 tsp vanilla extract - 1/4 cup (57g) butter, melted can use vegan butter for a vegan option Instructions 1. Add all ingredients to a high-speed blender and blend until smooth. 2. Remove and allow the batter to rest for 10 minutes. 3. Heat a skillet over medium heat, drop ¼ cup of batter into the skillet and cook until small bubbles appear. 4. Flip and continue to cook for another 3-4 minutes. 5. Remove and repeat until all batter has been used up. The batter makes about 10 pancakes. 6. Serve pancakes with your favorite pancake toppings. save this for your next slow weekend morning and share with a fellow mom who needs to try this!

tt-7650999023972764942.caption: Fast food isn’t necessarily the problem.  How often you eat it is.  Eating out is part of real life, so instead of pretending you’ll never hit a drive-thru, here’s how I actually think about it: Every day? Build a bowl. Chipotle, Cava, Sweetgreen, and Panera let you load up on protein and veggies and still be out the door in five minutes. Get the dressing on the side and only use 1/3 of it. Once a week? A burger, a burrito, a sub. Try to load them up with as many veggies as you can, and get the burger without the bun. Still satisfying, still completely fine.  Once a month? The Big Mac, the pizza, the Frosty. Yes, really. Treats stay treats when they aren’t an everyday thing. And treats in moderation can be part of a healthy diet. Balance was never about cutting foods out. It’s about how often they show up on your plate.  Save this for the next time you’re standing in line staring at the menu, and send it to whoever you always end up in the drive-thru with. 👇

tt-7656605663853890830.caption: @traderjoes had the prettiest figs the other day, so I turned them into an easy toddler freezer treat! 🍌✨ Ingredients: • 2 fresh figs, sliced (stem removed) • About ¾ banana, sliced (or use a whole banana) • Whole milk Greek yogurt • 1 @onceuponafarm Tractor Wheel, crumbled Directions: 1. Arrange the fig and banana slices on a plate or tray with parchment paper. 2. Spoon whole milk Greek yogurt over the fruit. 3. Sprinkle with crumbled Tractor Wheel pieces. 4. Freeze for a few hours until set. 5. Transfer to an airtight container and store in the freezer. To serve, let thaw for a few minutes before offering to your little one. 💛 A simple snack packed with fruit, protein, healthy fats, and fiber! ✨ Toddler tip: Figs are a great source of fiber, but if your little one is trying them for the first time, start with a small amount. I only gave my toddler 2 fig slices and added more banana slices since too much fiber at once can sometimes upset little tummies. Save this for later and follow for more easy toddler recipes and snack ideas! ✨ #easyrecipe #summertreats #toddlersnacks #toddlerfoodideas #figs

tt-7659494293077232910.caption: ✨ Easy Air Fryer Sweet Potato Stuffed Bites ✨ These bites are soft, cheesy, and packed with protein—perfect for little hands! It’s a plus not having to turn on the oven during the summer too 💛 🧡 Ingredients: • 1 cup mashed sweet potato • ½ cup all-purpose flour • Cooked ground beef, seasoned to your liking • Mozzarella cheese • Olive oil 👩🏻‍🍳 Directions: 1. Mix the mashed sweet potato and flour until a soft dough forms. Knead with your hands. 2. Roll into balls, then flatten each one. 3. Add a spoonful of seasoned ground beef and a little mozzarella cheese to the center. 4. Pinch the dough closed and roll back into a ball. 5. Place on parchment paper in your air fryer and brush the tops with olive oil. 6. Air fry at 325°F for 20 minutes, flipping halfway through (10 minutes per side), until lightly golden. The sweet potato bread will turn slightly brown and crack a little.  💡 Feel free to switch up the filling with whatever your toddler loves—shredded chicken, veggies, beans, or different cheeses all work great! ❤️ Save this recipe and like & follow for more simple toddler recipes! #easyrecipe #toddlermeals #toddlersnacks #toddlerlunch #toddlerdinner

tt-7668825782554234126.caption: RECIPE BELOW👇 These secret veggie packed donuts are a hit with my whole family, and taste amazing with only about 7 grams of added sugar per serving! Save this the next time you’re craving donuts and share with a friend who needs to try this! Follow for daily healthy recipes that taste just like your favorite treats! Ingredients:  1 banana 1/2 cup carrots 1/2 cup spinach 1 egg 1/4 cup maple syrup 2 tbsp melted coconut oil 1/4 tsp salt 1/2 tsp vanilla 1/4 cup cocoa powder + 1 tbsp 1 cup flour 1.5 tsp baking powder optional: 2 tbsp dairy free dark chocolate chips + 1 tsp melted coconut oil  Add banana, carrots, spinach, egg, maple syrup, 2 tbsp coconut oil, salt, and vanilla to a blender and blend until smooth Add the cocoa powder, flour and baking powder to a mixing bowl and mix until combined.  Add the blender batter to the mixing bowl with the flour and mix until just combined. Grease a donut pan with cooking spray (I like avocado oil cooking spray for this) Add your donut batter to the pan Bake 18-20 min at 350 degrees F  Melt dark chocolate chips + coconut oil in the microwave Drizzle over donuts Top with sprinkles Enjoy! #donuts #doughnut

tt-7673230653814623502.caption: Korean Japgokbap (잡곡밥) — Multigrain Rice An easy way to add more whole grains, fiber, and texture to your rice—and perfect for meal prepping! 💛 🌾 You’ll need: • 1 cup @Kim'C Market Organic 5 Colored Rice (Use link in bio under My Favorites or use code BUSYMAMAEASYBITES for $10 off)  • 2 cups short or medium-grain white rice • Filtered water Wash the 5 colored rice about 3 times, then soak for 30 minutes to help soften the outer layer of the grains. Add the white rice and wash everything together 3–4 more times, until the water runs mostly clear. Transfer to your rice cooker and add filtered water. I use the Korean hand method—place your hand flat over the rice and add water up to the knuckles where your fingers meet your palm. Cook on the multigrain setting (mine takes about 45 minutes), until the grains are tender. Fluff and mix! 🍚 To freeze: Scoop into ½-cup portions—I use a muffin tray—and freeze for a few hours before transferring to a labeled freezer bag. To reheat: Place a portion in a bowl, sprinkle with a little water, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave until piping hot all the way through.  Such an easy staple to have ready for busy nights! 🙌🏼 #Easyrecipe #Freezerprep #Mealprep #Koreanfood #koreanfoodlovers☺️🍶🍲🍜🍣

tt-7674995086555417870.caption: 🫐 2-Ingredient Blueberry Chia Jam for Toddlers 💙 So simple, naturally sweet, and perfect to keep on hand for PB&Js, toast, oatmeal, yogurt, pancakes, and more! Ingredients: • 1 cup fresh or frozen blueberries • 1 tbsp chia seeds • Optional sweetener — I skip it when the berries are nice and sweet! How to make it: Add the blueberries to a small saucepan and cook over low-medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until they burst and become soft and juicy. Gently mash them to your preferred texture. Turn off the heat, stir in 1 tbsp chia seeds, and let the jam sit for a few minutes. The chia seeds will soften and gel as the mixture cools, giving you that perfect jammy texture. 🫐 Store some in an airtight container in the fridge for the week, then freeze the rest in single-serve portions. I love having little portions ready to thaw whenever we want a quick PB&J. 🙌 #ToddlerRecipes #ToddlerMeals #ToddlerFood #easyrecipe #jam

tt-7675566140340391181.caption: Easy Toddler Blueberry Muffins 🍌🫐 Makes: about 12 mini muffins or 6 regular muffins Ingredients * 1 ripe banana, mashed * 1 egg * ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt  * 2 tablespoons melted butter or neutral oil * 1 teaspoon vanilla extract  * ¾ cup all-purpose flour * ½ teaspoon baking soda * ½ cup blueberries, fresh or frozen Directions 1. Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a mini muffin pan or use liners. 2. Mash the banana well. Stir in the egg, yogurt, melted butter, and vanilla. 3. Add flour and baking soda. Stir just until combined. 4. Gently fold in the blueberries. For younger toddlers, you can smush or chop larger blueberries. 5. Fill muffin cups. 6. Bake ~15 minutes for mini muffins or ~20-30 minutes for regular muffins, until a toothpick comes out clean. 7. Cool before serving.  #easyrecipe #toddlermeals #momrecipes❤️ #toddlerbreakfast #toddlersnack

tt-7676197216297553165.caption: #Ad  Would you put an entire avocado into chocolate muffins? 🥑🍫 Research has shown that as kids get older, they tend to eat fewer fruits and vegetables. Fresh avocados are one simple and delicious way to include more fruit in back-to-school meals and snacks.  Today I’m partnering with @aguacatesloveonetoday to make these Avocado Chocolate Muffins have become one of my favorite make-ahead snacks for busy school weeks. Fresh avocados are the star of this recipe, creating an incredibly soft, rich texture while contributing healthy unsaturated fats, fiber and more than 20 vitamins and minerals. Recipe Ingredients ● 1 ripe avocado ● ½ cup all purpose flour or oat flour ● 2 eggs ● ⅓ cup peanut butter ● ⅓ cup maple syrup ● ⅓ cup cocoa powder ● 1 tsp vanilla extract ● 1 tsp baking powder ● Handful of chocolate chips Directions 1. If using oat flour, blend the oats into a fine flour. 2. Add the avocado and all remaining ingredients except the chocolate chips, then blend until smooth. 3. Fold in the chocolate chips. 4. Pour into a greased muffin tin. 5. Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes. 6. Let cool completely before serving. Have you ever baked with avocado before? @Aguacates - Love One Today #loveonetoday

tt-7677063794421452046.caption: Korean toddler Gyeran Mari 🇰🇷🍳 Whenever I make gyeran mari (Korean rolled eggs), it brings back childhood memories 🥹 It’s such a classic Korean side dish, and now I love getting to make a simple toddler-friendly version for my daughter. Ingredients: 🥚 3 eggs 🥕 Finely chopped carrots 🌱 Finely chopped green onions 🧄 Sprinkle of garlic powder 🫒 Olive oil for the pan Whisk the eggs, then mix in the carrots, green onions, and garlic powder. Cook on low-medium heat in a lightly oiled pan. Pour in a thin layer of the egg mixture, fold one end over and begin rolling. Push the roll to one side, add more egg mixture, and continue rolling until you’ve used it all. Let it cool, then slice into toddler-friendly pieces! I served hers with little rice balls she could easily grab and eat. 🍚🤍 A little piece of my childhood, now on her plate. 🥹🇰🇷 #toddlerrecipes #toddlermeals #koreanfood #easyrecipe #toddlerfood

tt-7680031735425305869.caption: Toddler Breakfast Bites ✈️🍳 These were SO simple to make and honestly aren’t just for toddlers — they’re an easy breakfast for the whole family! I enjoy them too, which makes them perfect for meal prep when you don’t want to make separate breakfasts for everyone. We have an upcoming flight, and I’m planning to pack these for my toddler so we have something homemade, filling, and easy to eat instead of having to grab airport food. ✈️ Ingredients: ✨ 1 cup ground chicken 🥕 Optional: finely chopped carrots + mushrooms 🥚 3 eggs — 2 scrambled + 1 raw for binding 🧀 ¼ cup cottage cheese 🧀 ¼ cup shredded cheese 🥄 2 tbsp all-purpose flour My ground chicken already had finely chopped carrots and mushrooms mixed in from another meal, so I used that! You can totally leave the veggies out or add whatever finely chopped veggies you have on hand. How to make: Cook the ground chicken until fully cooked (along with the veggies if using). Scramble 2 eggs separately. Let everything cool slightly, then combine with 1 raw egg, cottage cheese, shredded cheese, and flour. Form into little bites/patties and bake at 350°F convection for 25 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the centers reach 165°F. Let them cool and enjoy! 🤍 Make a batch for the whole family or save them for an easy grab-and-go breakfast. Save this for your next busy morning or travel day! ✈️ #toddlerbreakfast #toddlerrecipes #toddlermeals #familybreakfast #easyrecipe
