video.narration: Hi, I'm tb and today was round 2 of IVF making a baby now involves needles and a small pharmacy in my fridge People get a little weird when I tell them we're going through IVF They get even weirder when I tell them I had three miscarriages and I get it People don't know what to say because they're terrified of saying the wrong thing grief is weird and everyone does it differently For me it was realizing my first child was an absolute miracle I just didn't know enough at the time. Another part was talking about what happened a lot and probably more than some people were prepared for But saying it out loud helped every time I told a story it felt less like a This terrible thing that happened to me and a little more like complaining about a delayed flight and kindness is what healed me Not perfectly chosen words. Maybe sharing everything was also my way of testing myself Can I say this out loud and still be okay? Can I say it without falling apart? Turns out yes, so I guess that's what grief looked like for me talking about it until the words stopped hurting and Letting a lot of very kind people say slightly awkward things

tt-7684065280766610701.caption: Toddler Korean Bulgogi Rice Balls 🇰🇷🍚✨ An easy Korean-inspired meal that my toddler can pick up and eat with her hands! These bulgogi rice balls are savory with a little natural sweetness from applesauce and come together so quickly. My toddler loves these, and they’re an easy way to get protein + veggies into one bite. 🤍 🥩 Ingredients: • 1 lb ground beef • ½ medium carrot, finely chopped • ½ medium onion, finely diced • 2 cloves garlic, minced • Finely diced mushrooms • 1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce • 1 tbsp sesame oil • 2 tbsp unsweetened applesauce • Sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds • Cooked rice • Olive oil for cooking You can also add in any finely chopped veggies you have on hand! 🍳 How to make them: 1. Sauté the garlic and onion in a little olive oil until fragrant. 2. Add the carrots and cook until they begin to soften. 3. Add the ground beef and cook through, breaking it into small pieces. I used a paper towel to carefully dab away any excess fat. 4. Add the finely diced mushrooms or any other finely chopped veggies you’d like. 5. Stir in the low-sodium soy sauce, sesame oil and applesauce. 6. Continue cooking until everything is fully cooked and combined, then sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. 7. Mix the bulgogi beef with cooked rice. 8. Once cool enough to handle, use your hands to form into toddler-sized rice balls. That’s it! 🙌 Easy, quick, and perfect for little hands. My toddler loves being able to pick these up and feed herself! Save this one for an easy toddler lunch or dinner! 🫶 #toddlerrecipes #toddlermeals #toddlerfood #koreanfood #easyrecipe

tt-7688538375174884622.caption: 🍤 Toddler Korean Shrimp Pancake or Jeon (새우전) My toddler LOVES foods she can hold herself right now — and if she can “dip dip” it into a sauce like ketchup, even better 😂 These little shrimp jeon are soft, easy to hold, and packed with shrimp + veggies! Ingredients: • 9 shrimp — I used @costco Argentine wild-caught shrimp • Finely chopped onion • Finely chopped zucchini • Finely chopped carrot • 1 egg • Garlic powder • 1–2 tbsp cornstarch or potato starch, as needed • Olive oil for cooking Directions: 1. Finely mince the raw shrimp into very small pieces. 2. Finely chop the onion, zucchini, and carrot. 3. Add the shrimp and veggies to a bowl with the egg, a sprinkle of garlic powder, and enough cornstarch or potato starch to help everything hold together. 4. Mix until well combined. 5. Heat a little olive oil in a pan over low-medium heat. 6. Spoon small portions into the pan and gently flatten into toddler-sized pancakes. 7. Cook on both sides until golden brown and the shrimp is fully cooked through. 8. Let cool and serve! We added ketchup for dipping because apparently everything tastes better when you can dip it. 😂 #easyrecipe #toddlermeals #momrecipes❤️ #toddlerdinner #toddlerrecipes

tt-7689259958264696077.caption: RECIPE BELOW👇 These frozen cotton candy grapes are sweet, sour, crunchy, and such a fun way to turn fresh fruit into a candy-like treat!  Save this the next time you’re craving something sweet and share with a friend who needs to try this! Follow for more healthy recipes that taste just like your favorite treats! recipe modified from @healthylittlepeach COTTON CANDY GRAPES  Makes 8 servings | about ½ cup per serving Ingredients * 4 cups green grapes, washed and dried * 1 cup granulated monk fruit sweetener  * Juice of 2 limes Instructions 1. Line a large baking sheet or dish with parchment paper. 2. Add the grapes and fresh lime juice to a large bowl. Toss until the grapes are evenly coated, then refrigerate for 10 minutes. 3. Remove the grapes from the refrigerator and roll each grape in the monk fruit sweetener mixture until completely coated. 4. Arrange the coated grapes in a single layer on the parchment-lined pan. 5. Freeze for 2–3 hours, or until completely frozen. 6. Grab a handful straight from the freezer and enjoy your “cotton candy”!  Estimated nutrition per serving (½ cup): ~50 calories | ~13g carbs | ~1g protein | 0g fat | ~1g fiber | 0g added sugar

tt-7691705534185098509.caption: The viral brothy beef bowl… but make it toddler-friendly 🤍 I made my own creamy version using @Kettle and Fire Beef Bone Broth and turned it into a dinner my toddler AND the rest of the family can enjoy. The broth is really what brings the whole bowl together 🙌 I used Kettle & Fire as the base to make it flavorful and comforting while keeping the recipe simple enough for a weeknight dinner. Save this one! 👇 Toddler-Friendly Creamy Brothy Beef Bowl Beef • 1 lb ground beef • 1 cup grated carrot • ½ tsp garlic powder • ½ tsp onion powder • ½ tsp paprika • Black pepper, optional Creamy broth • 2 cups  Beef Bone Broth • 1 tbsp tomato paste • 1 garlic clove, minced • ¼ cup heavy cream • ¼ cup finely shredded cheddar • ½ tsp Italian seasoning To serve: cooked rice + optional parsley How to make it: Brown the ground beef and grated carrot with the seasonings until cooked through and golden. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds, then add tomato paste and cook for 1–2 minutes. Pour in the Beef Bone Broth, add Italian seasoning, and simmer for 5 minutes. Lower the heat and stir in the heavy cream and cheddar until creamy. Add rice to your bowl, top with the beef, and ladle that creamy broth over everything. 🤍 For toddlers, I like adding enough broth to make the rice extra soft and saucy. For the adults, add cucumber, parsley, black pepper, or red pepper flakes. One dinner for the whole family 🙌 #kfpartner #toddlermeals #familydinner #toddlerrecipes #easyfamilymeals

tt-7697640013776833822.caption: Full recipe! You probably have all ingredients already 🍁✨ Apple Carrot Molasses Breakfast Cookies 🍎 These are a healthy, grab-and-go breakfast packed with fiber!  Ingredients Dry: - 3 cups flour (360g)  (I use spelt and einkorn, any flour will work here)  - 3 tsp cinnamon   - 1 tsp nutmeg   - ½ tsp ginger   - ¼ tsp cloves   - 1½ tsp baking powder   - 1 tsp baking soda   - 1 tsp salt   Wet: - 1⅓ cups coconut sugar (270g) or brown sugar   - ⅓ cup butter or coconut oil  - 2 large eggs   - ⅓ cup unsulphured molasses   - 1 tsp vanilla   Add-ins: - 2 cups shredded apples (firm sweet variety like Honeycrisp/Fuji)   -1 cup shredded carrots  -1 cup rolled oats  Instructions 1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment.   2. Whisk all dry ingredients in a bowl.   3. Beat wet ingredients on medium 2–3 min until smooth.  Add apple and carrot and oats.  4. Mix dry into wet until combined.   6. Scoop ¼-1/2 cup portions, space 2" apart on sheets.  - top with apple slices (optional)  7. Bake 12–14 min until edges lightly browned (check at 10 min for softer centers).   8. Cool on sheet 2–3 min, then transfer to rack.   Tips - Best slightly soft in middle — don’t overbake.   - Store airtight at room temp 3 days or freeze up to 3 months (microwave 20–30 sec to warm).   -Let a small piece of butter melt on top after baked #momof3 #breakfastideas #healthycooking #healthybaking #toddlerbreakfast

Always in caption :) Roasted Veggie & Bacon Pasta Salad Ingredients •  1 box (16 oz) pasta •  3 whole bell peppers, chopped •  1 large red onion, chopped •  1–2 cups halved Brussels sprouts •  Olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper •  3–4 slices bacon, chopped Cook the pasta according to package directions; drain and cool. Toss the peppers, onion, and Brussels sprouts with olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper, top with the chopped bacon, and roast at 350°F for about 30 minutes until tender. Combine the cooled pasta with the roasted veggies and bacon, then toss with the pumpkin vinaigrette. Add shaved Parmesan (about a cup)  Storage Keeps well in the fridge for 3–4 days in an airtight container—great for meal prep. Taste and adjust seasoning; thin with a splash of water if needed.#momof3 #healthycooking #dinnerideas #recipesoftiktok

steps: Preheat oven to 300°F.
Toast the bread cubes for 8-10 minutes to dry them out. Alternatively, you can use day old bread that is already dried out.
Increase oven temperature to 350°F.
Heat oil in a sauté pan. Add the sausage and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until slightly golden. Remove sausage to a large mixing bowl to cool.

In the same saute pan, add the butter and sauté the onions for 3 minutes. Add the celery, apples, and thyme and sauté for an additional 5 minutes, until everything is heated through and the veggies are tender. Allow to cool a few minutes before continuing.

Place the bread cubes, cooled sautéed vegetables and remaining ingredients into the large mixing bowl with the sausage and toss to thoroughly combine. (It's important that your ingredients are cool to the touch before adding the eggs so that they don't scramble.)
Spoon the stuffing mixture into greased muffin tins, filling all the way to the top. Pat the mixture down to pack it well.
Bake for 45 minutes or until the tops are just golden.

ingredients: 4 cups grated cheddar cheese (shred it yourself for best melting!)
1 pound elbow macaroni (you can also use campanelle, cavatappi, or shells)
steps: Place the topping ingredients in a bowl and stir to combine.
Preheat oven to 400° F.
Cook pasta in salted water* for about 3 minutes less than package directions call for, until al dente, reserving half a cup of the pasta water.
In a large pot melt the butter and then add the flour, whisking continuously over low-medium heat for 2-3 minutes to make a roux.
Slowly whisk in the milk and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, whisking occasionally, 3 to 4 minutes, or until sauce is gently bubbling and starting to thicken.
Add reserved pasta water and cheddar cheese and whisk until melted.
Stir in the pasta.
Transfer to a greased 9"x13" baking dish.
Sprinkle topping on macaroni and cheese.

ingredients: 1 pound rigatoni or favorite shaped pasta

steps: In a large pot, bring 4 quarts of water plus 1 tbsp of salt to a boil.
Cook the pasta according to package directions and drain reserving 1 cup of the pasta water.

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.

Place all the vegetables on a large baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and toss to coat all the vegetables and sprinkle with salt. Alternatively at this point you can place the vegetables in a large zipper bag and refrigerate overnight.
Roast for 45-50 minutes, stirring halfway through, or until tender and golden.

Serve with additional salt to taste.

yt-4JQEEtJaPdk.caption:
The best low sugar swaps that feel like dessert!! See the description for more details!
Prevent the 3pm sugar crash👇🏽

Most of the snacks marketed to families are designed to be grabbed fast and eaten faster.

The problem is they spike blood sugar, wear off in an hour, and leave kids irritable, distracted, and asking for something else ten minutes later.

These are the swaps we actually use in our house. Real food, naturally sweet, and easy enough to throw together on a Tuesday morning before school.

🐜 Ants on a log: celery sticks spread with peanut butter and topped with raisins. Done in two minutes. (Or make my "reindeer" version if your kids get bored of ants on a log!)
🍿 Creative homemade popcorn - add any toppings you like! My kids love just a little bit of caramel or sugar to make "kettle corn" but you really don't need a lot to add sweetness. 1 tsp is enough!
🍎 Apple slices with Peanut or Greek yogurt dip: slice an apple, mix plain Greek yogurt with a tiny drizzle of honey and a pinch of cinnamon. That's it. You can also do this with peanut butter mixed with a tiny drizzle of honey for sweetness.
🌰 Energy bites: Take rolled oats + any nut butter + any toppings your kids like (my kids like dried fruit + chocolate chips). Roll them into balls, chill in the fridge, enjoy all week!
🥣 Yogurt bowls: Better than fro-yo! My kids love Greek yogurt topped with berries, granola, nut butter and a drizzle of honey. 
🫐 Blueberry cobbler: frozen blueberries microwaved for 60 seconds, topped with a handful of oats, a drizzle of maple syrup, and a pinch of cinnamon. Feels like dessert, works as a snack.

Same fun. A fraction of the sugar.

And the kind of snack that actually keeps kids full until the next meal.

You don't have to be a plant-based family to make these work for yours.

And when you are hungry? Snack smart with simple whole-food pairings #shorts
Hydration = your secret superpower! 💧
So often we think we're hungry when we're really just thirsty. Sip throughout the day (aim for ~64 oz!) to boost energy, digestion, and curb cravings.

And when you are hungry? Snack smart with simple whole-food pairings:
🥕 Veggies + hummus
🍎 Apple + peanut butter
🍓 Fruit + Greek yogurt

Easy, healthy, no prep — my fave kind of snack! 💚

#healthytips #hydration101 #smartsnacking
yt-En5mA4ZYuqY.creator: thepickyeater
yt-En5mA4ZYuqY.summary: And when you are hungry? Snack smart with simple whole-food pairings Hydration = your secret superpower!
yt-En5mA4ZYuqY.title: Veggies + hummus

video.narration: Hydrate and snack smart. Now, I think everybody is staying pretty well hydrated. I mean, everyone has a water bottle these days, but really hydration is the key to knowing when you're actually hungry because sometimes when you're feeling hungry, you're actually thirsty. So I always recommend just if you're not already carrying around a water bottle, sticking small sips throughout the day and aiming for at least 64 ounces of water a day. So that's like eight cups of water a day. Drinking water not only provides the benefit of being hydrated, but it helps support energy and digestion. And when it comes to snacks, my biggest tip is to pick something that basically is like one word, like a fruit or a vegetable and then pairing that with something that's a protein. So veggies and hummus, fruit and nuts, or apples and peanut butter, Greek yogurt and fruit. These are all whole food protein pairings that will help keep you full and are healthy options that require no prep.

Top 4 Nutrition Hacks From A Gluten-Free Vegan Health Coach💚
1️⃣ Rolled oats instead of processed breakfast cereals 

Why? Many cereals are full of refined flours, added sugars, and artificial additives. Rolled oats are gluten-free, nutrient-dense, and a healthier choice! 🌱

2️⃣ Tempeh instead of processed plant-based meats 

Processed vegan meats can have refined flours, hydrogenated oils, and excess salt. Tempeh is a fermented, protein-packed, and fiber-rich option. 💪

3️⃣ Whole grain gluten-free bread instead of white bread

White bread is made with refined flour that spikes blood sugar and lacks nutrients. Whole grain bread is full of fiber and keeps you satisfied for longer! 🍞

4️⃣ Homemade hummus instead of store-bought spreads

Many store-bought spreads contain unhealthy oils, additives, and too much salt. Homemade hummus is fresh, simple, and healthier! 🥙

Sweet Potato Brown Sugar and Cinnamon Graham Crackers ✨❤️😋   200 g all-purpose flour (about 1⅔ cups) + 2 tablespoons  •  170 g whole wheat flour (about 1½ cups) •  1 tsp baking soda •  1½ tsp cinnamon •  ¼ tsp nutmeg (optional) •  ½ tsp kosher salt •  8 oz (226 g / 2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened •  5 oz (142 g) dark brown sugar, packed •  2 Tbsp maple syrup  •  150 g cooked, mashed sweet potato (about ⅔ cup), cooled and fairly dry(roast or steam, then mash; blot with paper towel if watery) •  Optional topping: 2 Tbsp butter + dark brown sugar + 1½ tsp cinnamon  1.  Heat oven to 350°F. 2.  Whisk both flours, baking soda, cinnamon,, and salt. 3.  Cream butter, brown sugar, and syrup until smooth (not fluffy). 4.  Mix in the mashed sweet potato until even. 5.  Add dry ingredients on low speed. The dough will look crumbly at first, then darken. Squeeze a handful: it should hold like pie dough.  •  Too dry / won’t clump: add 1 Tbsp very soft butter.  •  Too sticky: add 1–2 Tbsp AP flour.Don’t add water or milk. 6.  Divide onto 2 sheets of parchment. Shape each into a compact rectangle. If sticky, chill 30–60 minutes. 7.  Cover with more parchment and roll to about ⅛ inch (3 mm). yt-QS3a6dYsryc.caption:
The biggest misconceptions about veganism 🌱 Read the caption! #shorts
While a vegan lifestyle can be incredibly nourishing and packed with health benefits, simply cutting out animal products doesn’t guarantee a balanced diet.

A healthy vegan diet still requires planning and an understanding of essential nutrients. Here’s why:
- Protein Matters: When you’re eating vegan, protein can be trickier to get, but it’s still key for energy, muscle health, and feeling full. Adding foods like lentils, tofu, quinoa, and chickpeas ensures you’re getting enough of this essential macronutrient.
- Healthy Fats Are Essential: Many vegan diets can be low in healthy fats, which are critical for brain function, hormone balance, and energy. Avocados, nuts, seeds, and olive oil are great sources of these fats.
- Balanced Nutrition: Whole foods, veggies, and fruits are the base of a healthy vegan diet, but variety matters too. To avoid relying on processed vegan options, fill your meals with colorful produce, whole grains, and plant-based proteins.

Eating vegan doesn’t mean automatic health—it’s about making smart food choices and ensuring your body gets the nutrients it needs to thrive. So if you’re vegan or considering going vegan, take the time to learn about balanced, nutrient-rich meals.

yt-bIJfm5JbmAc.caption:
Does your child love candy? Remember these 3 things! 🍫 #shorts
Control over timing - by deciding when your child can have candy, you can avoid sugar rushes at the worst times, like right before bed or during school hours. 

Pair candy with protein - when candy is paired with a protein, like nuts or milk, it slows the sugar absorption, helping your child avoid the highs and lows of a sugar crash. 

Avoid the “Forbidden Fruit” effect - letting your kids enjoy candy without a lot of restrictions makes it less of a “forbidden fruit.” This helps them develop a healthier relationship with sweets, where candy isn’t off-limits, but just another treat they can enjoy when properly balanced with other foods.

Full recipe! You probably have all ingredients already 🍁✨

Apple Carrot Molasses Breakfast Cookies 🍎
These are a healthy, grab-and-go breakfast packed with fiber! 

Ingredients
Dry:
- 3 cups flour (360g)  (I use spelt and einkorn, any flour will work here) 
- 3 tsp cinnamon  
- 1 tsp nutmeg  
- ½ tsp ginger  
- ¼ tsp cloves  
- 1½ tsp baking powder  
- 1 tsp baking soda  
- 1 tsp salt  

Wet:
- 1⅓ cups coconut sugar (270g) or brown sugar  
- ⅓ cup butter or coconut oil 
- 2 large eggs  
- ⅓ cup unsulphured molasses  
- 1 tsp vanilla  

Add-ins:
- 2 cups shredded apples (firm sweet variety like Honeycrisp/Fuji)  
-1 cup shredded carrots 
-1 cup rolled oats 

Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment.  
2. Whisk all dry ingredients in a bowl.  
3. Beat wet ingredients on medium 2–3 min until smooth.  Add apple and carrot and oats. 
4. Mix dry into wet until combined.  
6. Scoop ¼-1/2 cup portions, space 2" apart on sheets.  - top with apple slices (optional) 
7. Bake 12–14 min until edges lightly browned (check at 10 min for softer centers).  
8. Cool on sheet 2–3 min, then transfer to rack.  

Tips
- Best slightly soft in middle — don’t overbake.  
- Store airtight at room temp 3 days or freeze up to 3 months (microwave 20–30 sec to warm).  
-Let a small piece of butter melt on top after baked  #toddlerbreakfast #healthybaking #breakfastideas #momof3 #busymom

•  1 tablespoon grainy mustard

5 Signs You’re Not Eating Enough ‼️
Not eating enough can lead to some serious symptoms that affect your energy, mood, and overall health. 

Here's how to spot it and fix it: 🍽️
1) Constant fatigue – If you're always tired, it could mean you're not getting enough calories or nutrients. Try adding more protein, healthy fats, and whole grains to your meals to boost energy. 💪
2) Irritability & mood swings – Low blood sugar from under-eating can cause mood shifts. Keep snacks like nuts or fruit handy to stabilize your blood sugar levels throughout the day. 🍎
3) Hair loss or thinning – Lack of key nutrients like iron and vitamins can cause hair issues. Focus on nutrient-dense foods like leafy greens, nuts, and eggs. 🥗
4) Difficulty concentrating – Not eating enough can affect your brain function. Eat regular, balanced meals to improve focus and clarity. 🧠
5) Frequent hunger pangs – Always hungry? This means your body isn’t getting the fuel it needs. Add more fiber and protein-rich foods to stay full longer. 🍗
Fix this by eating nutrient-dense meals consistently. Start nourishing your body right today

Full recipe here! Always in caption :) 

Banana hazelnut chocolate granola bars 

Adding a banana and roasting it with your granola makes the loveliest flavor! 

1 ripe banana
3/4 cup of oats
2.5 cups of chopped almonds and hazelnuts
1 cups of pumpkin seed
1/2 cup raisins or dried cranberries
2/3 cup nut butter
1/3 cup maple syrup
1/2 cup coconut oil
Salt to taste

Combine all and bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 20 minutes or until golden brown
Cover with chocolate and cut! That’s it!

Chocolate topping (optiona)l:
1.5 cups of chocolate
.5 cips coconut oil

Picky Eating Isn’t Just A Phase ⚠️
Dealing with picky eaters can be challenging, but with the right approach, you can encourage healthier eating habits. 

1) Start by introducing new foods gradually and pairing them with familiar favorites. 

2) Make mealtime enjoyable by involving your child in meal prep and letting them choose between options.

3) Keep portions small to avoid overwhelming them, and avoid pressure or negativity around food. 

Remember, it’s about creating a positive relationship with food, so celebrate small victories and remain patient.

Want more tips for dealing with picky eaters? Follow me for helpful advice and easy recipes!

video.narration: Craving comfort food? Let's make creamy carrot potato soup in under 45 minutes. Start by sautéing onions and garlic, then toss in carrots, potatoes, celery, and a sprinkle of Italian herbs. Add veggie broth and bay leaves, then let it simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. Blend half for that creamy texture, stir it back in, season to taste, and let it simmer a few more minutes. Serve it warm and enjoy every cozy, comforting spoonful. Grab the full recipe
steps: Start by sautéing onions and garlic, then toss in carrots, potatoes, celery, and a sprinkle of Italian herbs.
Add veggie broth and bay leaves, then let it simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Blend half for that creamy texture, stir it back in, season to taste, and let it simmer a few more minutes.
Serve it warm and enjoy every cozy, comforting spoonful.
